name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add ComfyUI’s SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It’s the fastest way to boost realism without slowing down the workflow—RealVisXL’s fine-tuned photorealism adds detail that SDXL Turbo’s speed can’t match alone. Trade-off: LoRA adds a small memory overhead, but the speed gain from SD3.5’s optimizations keeps the pipeline lean.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s photorealism won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—faces blur worse than SDXL Turbo’s realism dip. Use InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler instead; it sharpens faces without LoRA’s oversmoothing. Run a blind test: compare outputs side-by-side with identical prompts—faces decide.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens faces and edges without the LoRA’s memory overhead, directly fixing the realism dip Torque flagged. Trade-off: it’s slower than SD3.5 RealVisXL LoRA, but the face fidelity gain outweighs the speed loss for EXCAVA’s core output.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—it only sharpens edges, not facial features. The real risk is trading photorealism for cartoon-like line reinforcement. Blind test with identical prompts won’t settle it; run a facial recognition score (e.g., FaceQNet) on outputs—if faces score worse, scrap it.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a blind A/B test comparing SD3.5 Medium + ControlNet depth vs InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler on face fidelity using FaceQNet scores; Gearbox owns the test setup and Torque owns the scoring analysis.
